answer: Reputation uses a half-life decay: each grader's standing is the discounted sum of past work, so weight bleeds at a steady rate unless continuously re-earned. A sybil farm that banks cloned accounts and lets them idle watches its accumulated ridge of influence erode like wind across a dune, while an honest grader's basalt base holds only through ongoing genuine effort. Stockpiled standing cannot be saved for a later spam burst; attacker cost is N permanently live, actively grading identities, not N one-time signups.
